item_taken.first_six_words: Both ends named: once the enumerator
item_taken.why: The stall is made of the axis's endpoints: the plan named the line 'from the spring to the tide', wrote its last line as 'reach nine, where the fresh water runs out; expect the salt-tolerant end of every row', admitted the flounder as that end-member, and the report closed 'spring to tide, is complete' while the river ran two further kilometres to the sea holding six marine species; the walk closed on its named end and the subject stayed open. Not Stops on its best (2), because the flounder was called for by the framing, not hidden by it, and she stopped at the weir because the line ended there, not because the find satisfied her; not Missing column (16), because the six species below the weir sit past the axis's end and could be placed on the same line extended, not on an axis the box lacks; not Every address visited (13), because the twenty-seven cells were not given containers but a named line folded by habitat, and the members absent are absent past the line's end, not for lack of a container; not Box without a hole (9), because the grid was declared before sampling and had an empty cell.

reasoning: The rule splits the same axis into two sides: what the named axis produces, the limiting members it conscripts at its ends, is form-yields'; the walk that closes on those ends while the subject stays open is enumeration-stalls'. The case holds a produced member with its own dated facts: the line 'from the spring to the tide' folded into a nine-by-three grid, the one empty cell at the ninth reach's pool, its neighbours full on three sides (stickleback in the riffle, eel in the backwater, the pool column running trout, grayling, chub, bream, roach, stiller and warmer at each step), the notebook of 11 January 2021 predicting a bottom-living, salt-taking fish, a flounder or a goby, and the seine of 14 June 2021 taking three juvenile flounder. That member is the axis's tide end conscripted into the list before it was caught, so the rule places it on form-yields' side, and form-yields' of-sentence has the cell for it: a cell the pile's neighbours fix on every side, vouched for by the neighbours and the full cells. The closing of the report at the weir and the six marine species the 2024 team took below it are the walk closing on the end while the subject stays open, which the rule keeps here. The rule decides, and the case crosses as the yield; the closing facts travel with it as facts the case holds, not as the target's mechanism.
case_out: A form imposed on a pile: Hanne Rask, a freshwater ecologist surveying the fishes of the river Vael from 2019 to 2021, laid the survey in March 2019 on one named axis, 'from the spring to the tide', in nine reaches from the spring at Kell to the tidal weir at Orm, and folded the line into three rows by habitat, riffle, pool, and backwater, a grid of twenty-seven cells, each to be netted and its species entered. The plan's last line conscripted the axis's tide end in advance: reach nine, where the fresh water runs out; expect the salt-tolerant end of every row. What the form made visible: by the close of the 2020 season twenty-six cells held at least one species and one was empty, the pool of the ninth reach, the last above the weir, fixed by its neighbours on three sides, the ninth reach's riffle holding the three-spined stickleback, the ninth reach's backwater holding the eel, and the pool column running reach by reach from trout through grayling and chub to the bream and roach of the eighth reach, stiller and warmer at every step. The member the form produced: on 11 January 2021 she wrote, 'Reach 9 pool. Something lives here. Bottom-living, still water, takes the salt that comes up on spring tides: a flounder, or a goby. Look at low water in June,' and on 14 June 2021, seining the ninth-reach pool at low water, she took three juvenile flounder, a marine flatfish that ascends rivers, writing that evening, 'The sea comes up the Vael.' The tell that the form rather than the pile produced the item: the fish was described from the empty cell and its three full neighbours five months before it was caught, and it is the salt-tolerant end the plan's last line had ordered for every row. Her final report of October 2021 lists thirty species, the flounder last admitted and the only marine one, gives every one of the twenty-seven cells an occupant, and closes: the fauna of the Vael, spring to tide, is complete. Below the weir the river runs two further kilometres to the sea; the report does not sample it. In 2024 a second team netting the weir pool and the reach below it took mullet, bass, smelt, sand goby, sprat, and sand smelt, six marine species, none in her list. The same axis whose tide end yielded the flounder closed the walk at the weir; the closing is the stall the sending map keeps, and these facts travel with the case as its own.
